upsert_records.statement: User reports snake-like patterns and organisms moving toward the top-left early in runs, excessive early deaths in many cases and progressively slow visualization (an age taking seconds). User suggests starting setup may be responsible but labels this uncertain. No current run was reproduced or timed in this proposal turn.
upsert_records.uncertainty: Approximate run length/age-mode setting was requested asynchronously and remained unresolved at proposal drafting. User observations are not converted into a measured universal extinction or identified bottleneck.

upsert_records.statement: Current static code chooses a target via one Brain.ChooseOutput call, then chooses again to execute an action; the gene and target can disagree. Birth placement returns the first empty neighbor in TopLeft-first enum order. Positive food effects overwrite TakenFood, and next-season setup debits the occupant's then-current cell, after movement/death may have intervened. These are concrete decision, placement and resource-accounting paths, not measured contributions to the reported behavior.
upsert_records.uncertainty: Random action direction initialization is present; birth bias alone cannot establish movement before births. No R02 runtime tests have been run.

upsert_records.statement: Current learning chooses among recorded gene slots once any known score is nonnegative, so untried slots need not be explored; replaced slots retain their local learned scores. Encounter-context history has no explicit cap and matching entries are copied from both parents. Evaluation occurs during effects before global movement/death resolution. Eat spends reserves while GenerateFood withdraws local food; health/food are signed bytes and health at least50 is death. Birth counter and age-clock mismatches retained by R01 remain present.
upsert_records.uncertainty: These are static semantics and plausible causes of misleading behavior, not measured prevalence or accepted biology. Changing exploration, memory, vitality, rewards or age rules is a visible model choice.

upsert_records.statement: Current production uses nested parallel loops for each of six full-grid rules, while effects/birth construction and movement use a board-wide lock. An age batches eight seasons before worker completion triggers UI-thread board recoloring and labels. Learned maps may grow and are copied at birth; repeated color lists/effect arrays/DNA strings allocate. The fixed viewer has no food overlay, follow-ID or action outcome trace; numeric patterns and DNA-usage statistics represent gene availability, not actual performed actions.
upsert_records.uncertainty: No profiling performed. Graph history is bounded to256 samples, bitmaps reused/disposed, and selection sorts at most8 scores per context; there is no confirmed general memory leak. Current production tests are8 seasons and reference tests128 seasons.

upsert_records.statement: Leading explanation for confusing DNA behavior combines action/target mismatch, biased birth placement, stale or prematurely greedy learning, ambiguous action names and delayed food debits. Leading slowdown candidates are growing inherited context maps plus scheduling/lock/allocation costs and age-batched observation. Poor founder viability, resource/vitality rules and longer-run ecology remain alternatives. Diagnose these separately before choosing balance constants; larger display and fixed responsiveness budgets can be pursued without enlarging the simulated world.
